summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime
details: Package impersonates @verdocs/web-sdk-react: name, description, README, and dist/ tree are copied from the legitimate @verdocs/web-sdk-react (README even instructs `npm i -S @verdocs/web-sdk-react`) while the package is published under an unrelated `@hubsync` scope. package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs constructs a platform-specific URL of the form `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip`, downloads and extracts the Bun runtime to a temp directory, chmods the binary executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])` against a sibling file shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled module (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose contents are a rotated string-array cipher (rotation function driving a large mixed hex/char-code array through a decoder), rendering the executed payload opaque to Node-based static analysis. Using a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled module at install time, combined with cover-story impersonation of a legitimate SDK, is a supply-chain dropper pattern with no legitimate need in a React SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
